newsitem.title: GERMANY: German shares seek strength to break 3,800 in DAX.
newsitem.headline: German shares seek strength to break 3,800 in DAX.

text.p: German shares played catch-up to overnight Wall Street gains in early dealings on Wednesday as the market sought strength and higher trading volumes to break 3,800 points in the blue-chip DAX index.
The IBIS DAX, which reflects all-day computer dealings, was up 24.00 points at 3,785.07 points and near the high reached so far at 3,786.53 points.
Traders said any break above 3,800 points would require much stronger interest in the market since recent gains have come mainly from top DAX index shares such as Deutsche Bank AG and Siemens AG.
"The gains have mainly come from the top DAX stocks. A lot more stocks must participate in any rally if we want to break 3,800 points," said one dealer.
Many dealers were also squaring their books ahead of the close of the second quarter, which should help to underpin the DAX index in the near-term.
"There's no reason for the market to show any signs of weakness," the trader said. "The upward trend is still intact."
Among specific shares, carmaker Volkswagen AG was down 1.50 marks at 1,243 marks after reaching a deal with IG Metall over wages and part-time guidelines for older workers.
Technical factors dominated other major DAX components, including Deutsche Bank AG, which was up 1.40 marks at 103.25 marks following a four percent gain on Tuesday.
Some traders said Deutsche shares have a near-term potential of reaching 106 marks but noted that other major bank shares were not participating as heavily in the sector gains.
Electronics group Siemens AG was down 15 pfennigs at 107.35 marks on a small bout of profit-taking after rising about three percent in bourse trade on Tuesday.
"It's not too bad that Siemens is taking a breather," said one Frankfurt trader.
But other traders said Siemens still has a near-term target of 110 marks based on technical chart factors and said the modest pullback was no sign of an end to the gains.
Sportswear group Adidas AG was up 20 pfennigs at 198.80 marks after falling 1.50 marks to 198.50 marks on Tuesday on profit-taking.
Adidas shares have been gaining on speculation it may be chosen in July to join the DAX in September, a move that would prompt buying from investors seeking to balance portfolios.
